nodes.label: Multi-destination fare board
nodes.rationale: Existing sites show the date grid one destination at a time, turning a comparison into a dozen-tab exercise; this shows many destinations side by side, each as its own departure x return price matrix.

nodes.label: 'Around these dates' mode
nodes.source_location: Two ways to read the dates
nodes.rationale: The two date fields are anchors, each +/- window_days; the grid is departure x return around them.

nodes.label: 'Anywhere in this range' mode
nodes.source_location: Two ways to read the dates
nodes.rationale: The two fields bound a period and the Nights box says what to look for inside it; anchors cannot express this because two dates 56 days apart can only describe ~56-night trips. Range mode is far cheaper to fetch: one Kiwi calendar call per trip length, ~2 calls per destination instead of a whole grid. Coverage is reported against what was actually asked for, not the whole triangle.

nodes.label: Departure x return grid layout
nodes.source_location: Two ways to read the dates
nodes.rationale: Layout stays departure x return in both modes. In range mode priced cells form a diagonal band and the rest render plain rather than hatched. An earlier version compacted this to departure x trip-length; it was rejected because seeing the real calendar shape matters more than saving space.

nodes.label: run.py
nodes.rationale: Binds 127.0.0.1 by default so nothing off the machine can reach it; picks a free port, prints the URL and opens a browser.

nodes.label: serve.cmd
nodes.rationale: It is a .cmd, not a .ps1, because group policy sets AllSigned for Windows PowerShell here, so an unsigned script will not run; batch files are not subject to execution policy. The firewall rule is scoped to the domain profile so the port stays closed on home and public Wi-Fi. Binds 0.0.0.0 and serves inbound TCP 8712.

nodes.label: No authentication
nodes.rationale: Current build has no auth: anyone who can route to the host can run searches.

nodes.label: Single-process constraint
nodes.rationale: Search progress is streamed from an in-memory registry (app._streams), so a second uvicorn worker would answer some stream requests with 'unknown search id'. Do not add --workers.

nodes.label: Shared rate limiter and cache
nodes.rationale: Reason to host centrally rather than have everyone run their own copy: the Kiwi pacing lock is process-global so a single server cannot stampede the provider, and one person's filled grid is served to the next person from SQLite. Flip side is throughput: a 20-destination board is ~300 provider calls paced at 0.8s, about 4-5 minutes, and concurrent searches queue behind each other.

nodes.label: SQLite WAL mode
nodes.rationale: WAL mode with a 5s busy timeout so one user's board fill does not block another user's reads.

nodes.label: Travelpayouts token
nodes.rationale: Free, from travelpayouts.com; no website, traffic or approval required. fast-flights needs no key at all.

nodes.label: Independent per-matrix scroll viewport
nodes.source_location: Two ways to read the dates
nodes.rationale: Each matrix is its own scroll viewport in both axes, sized independently of the grid, so a card stays compact however wide the window gets. Date headers stay pinned; scroll position survives a re-render; page does not scroll when a grid hits its end (overscroll-behavior: contain).

nodes.label: On-demand window widening
nodes.source_location: Two ways to read the dates
nodes.rationale: Window starts at +/-7 days and grows on demand to FM_MAX_WINDOW_DAYS (default +/-28, a 57x57 grid). Grows via the +/- Nd button or by pushing ~160px past an edge (the 'pull for more' gesture). Reaching an edge deliberately does nothing because widening costs live API calls and Kiwi rate-limits, so it must never fire by accident.

nodes.label: Widening cost model (one call per trip length)
nodes.source_location: Why widening costs what it costs
nodes.rationale: One Kiwi calendar call = one trip length, covering the whole departure window (verified: 15/31/43/60/90 days returns exactly that many dates). Call count depends only on how many trip lengths the window spans. A +/-W window around an A-night trip spans lengths max(0, A-2W)..A+2W: 22 diagonals at +/-7, 50 at +/-21. Only 0 nights comes back genuinely empty. FM_KIWI_NIGHTS_CEILING (60) guards a runaway window; FM_KIWI_MAX_DIAGONALS caps fetching, keeping lengths nearest the anchor.

nodes.label: Per-matrix rank colour scale
nodes.rationale: A rank scale computed per matrix: each card runs from its own cheapest cell (green) to its own dearest (red), so colours answer 'which dates are good for this destination'. Colour does not compare across cards. Compare destinations by headline price, cheapest-first ordering, and the board-wide cheapest marker. Per-matrix scaling means every card uses the full ramp and its internal structure is readable, at the cost of cross-card comparability (green cut off at 1600 on one card and 4300 on another).

nodes.label: Hatched cell (no cached data)
nodes.rationale: Hatched = no cached data for that date pair; it does not mean expensive. Missing cells are hatched and excluded from the colour scale rather than left blank because gaps cluster on the odd off-peak combos that are often cheapest. Click to fetch that one cell live.

nodes.label: Table view
nodes.rationale: Lists every priced cell as sortable text, cheapest first; the real backstop when colour fails.

nodes.label: 'Only destinations' filter
nodes.rationale: Set before Search it restricts the search itself so the destination budget is spent inside the filter (IT searches the cheapest Italian cities); typed after a search it narrows the display instantly with no API calls. Matching is by IATA code, city, country code or country name. Codes match exactly and names by substring, deliberately, because substring-matching a two-letter code against country names over-matches badly (IT is inside Lithuania and United Kingdom, inflating one search from 7 to 16 matches).

nodes.label: Time-of-day windows (search parameters)
nodes.rationale: Depart between / Return between are search parameters, not display filters, because the price calendar returns only a date and a price with no departure time, so there is nothing to filter client-side. Narrowing the window genuinely reprices the board. A filtered search bypasses the cell cache in both directions: it does not reuse it (cache keyed on route/dates/currency only, so it would hand back unfiltered prices) nor write into it (which would poison it for later unfiltered searches).

nodes.label: Day-of-week and trip-length constraints
nodes.rationale: A view over cells already loaded, so instant and free. The colour scale, each card's cheapest cell and the board ordering all recompute over only the matching cells, so it answers 'cheapest Thu->Sun' rather than merely hiding rows. Excluded cells fade rather than vanish.

nodes.label: Cross-hair cell hover
nodes.rationale: Hovering a cell lights its departure column and return row and bolds both date headers so outbound vs return is never ambiguous; clicking pins it.

nodes.label: Locate button (per card)
nodes.rationale: Scrolls a grid to its own cheapest cell and pulses it, then names the price and dates in the status bar; on a widened grid the winner is usually scrolled out of sight.

nodes.label: Cell-click flight times (/api/details)
nodes.rationale: Clicking a cell fetches flight times from the board source via /api/details, in parallel with the Google cross-check. Returns both legs with local times, flight numbers, carriers, stops and duration, and works at any horizon including dates Google has no data for. The block is labelled with its source and price because each source's cheapest itinerary is often a different flight, so two unlabelled departure times would look like a contradiction.

nodes.label: Filter-carrying booking links
nodes.rationale: Booking links carry passenger counts and, when Nonstop only is on, Kiwi's direct-only flag stopNumber=0. Without that the booking page opens showing one-stop options, which reads as the filter being ignored. If a cell cannot be cross-checked the panel still shows the board's own price and a booking link from the source that priced it, rather than only a dead Google link.

nodes.label: Kiwi.com board source
nodes.rationale: The best free source found, needs no key and no signup. The only free source that returns real party totals for the actual passenger mix rather than a single-adult fare to scale up. Measured 95% (often 100%) mean coverage vs Travelpayouts 25%. Default; set FM_BOARD_PROVIDER=travelpayouts to switch back.

nodes.label: Kiwi umbrella GraphQL endpoint
nodes.rationale: api.skypicker.com/umbrella/v2/graphql; Kiwi's open umbrella GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.label: returnOnePerCityItineraries
nodes.rationale: ~70 destinations from TLV with real 2-adult-3-child prices in one call; used for discovery.

nodes.label: returnItineraryPricesCalendar
nodes.rationale: 15 dated prices per call. Pin nightsCount to a single value and each call fills one diagonal of the departure x return matrix, so ~22 calls give a complete grid. visibleDates is mandatory and may be combined with only one of nightsCount / departureDates / returnDates, which is why the fill is diagonal.

nodes.label: Diagonal grid fetching
nodes.source_location: Kiwi rate limiting, and how it is handled
nodes.rationale: Each Kiwi calendar call fills one diagonal (one trip length). Diagonal fetching is deliberately NOT capped any more: capping it left widened grids with a large unfilled band, which is a worse problem than the extra calls.

nodes.label: Virtual interlining
nodes.rationale: Kiwi does virtual interlining, so some cheap results are self-transfer combinations on separate tickets: legitimate, but a missed connection is the traveller's problem, not the airline's.

nodes.label: Kiwi rate limiting (403 blocking)
nodes.source_location: Kiwi rate limiting, and how it is handled
nodes.rationale: Kiwi blocks bursts by IP with a bare 403, no Retry-After, and the block lasts minutes. It is volume-based: while blocked even a trivial {__typename} 403s. The block applies to search operations; cheap queries recover first. Re-querying is the main way the limit gets tripped; hammering Search keeps the window open.

nodes.label: Filled-grid cache reuse
nodes.source_location: Kiwi rate limiting, and how it is handled
nodes.rationale: The main lever against rate limiting. A filled grid is stored and reused for FM_KIWI_CACHE_HOURS (default 6). Reuse requires the cached grid to be nearly complete for the window being asked for (FM_CACHE_REUSE_MIN_FRACTION, default 0.85 of valid cells), not just a minimum cell count: a flat count is unsafe because a grid written under an older narrower fetch strategy clears '20 cells' while missing whole diagonals and would be served forever. Measured symptom: a Larnaca grid stuck at 85/180 (47%) missing every trip length under 7 nights; with the fraction check it refetches to 170/180 (94%).

nodes.label: Kiwi call pacing
nodes.source_location: Kiwi rate limiting, and how it is handled
nodes.rationale: FM_KIWI_MIN_INTERVAL (0.8s) between calls, FM_KIWI_WORKERS (2) concurrency.

nodes.label: Shared rate-limit backoff (wait it out visibly)
nodes.source_location: Kiwi rate limiting, and how it is handled
nodes.rationale: On a 403 the provider backs off 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 45s up to FM_KIWI_WAIT_BUDGET (default 180s), streaming a status message so a pause reads as waiting rather than hanging. The block state is shared across threads, so a grid fill pauses once as a whole instead of each worker burning the budget separately.

nodes.label: Travelpayouts fallback (last resort)
nodes.source_location: Kiwi rate limiting, and how it is handled
nodes.rationale: Only after the wait budget is spent does it drop to Travelpayouts, and it says so, because the prices change meaning from real party totals to scaled estimates.

nodes.label: Travelpayouts / Aviasales Data API board fill
nodes.rationale: A cache of fares real Aviasales users saw over the last 2-7 days. The only free source that can answer 'where can I even go from TLV' in a single call. No passenger parameter, so a family total is extrapolated; rows past expires_at are dropped outright.

nodes.label: Search-driven coverage collapse
nodes.rationale: Cached rows exist only where real people searched, so coverage collapses the further ahead you look: mean 43% at 14 days out, 2% at 150. The tool is genuinely useful inside about two months and close to useless past four. Coverage also varies hugely by route (Rome 54%, Larnaca 49%, Varna 3% on one run). The board warns you when your window is far enough out to be sparse.

nodes.label: Family-total extrapolation (FM_CHILD_FACTOR)
nodes.rationale: Travelpayouts rows are single-ticket prices with no child fare, so a family total is extrapolated as price * (adults + children * FM_CHILD_FACTOR), FM_CHILD_FACTOR default 1.0. Checked live vs Google Flights (2 adults + 3 children, 3 weeks out): the cheapest cell was +62% mean, the median cell +35%. A typical cell is roughly a third under the real family price; the cheapest cell is systematically worse because the cheapest cached fare is exactly the one likely to have a seat or two left. This means the ranking itself is not trustworthy: Larnaca led at 1,010 and verified at 3,043, putting it last. Reproduce with data/estimate_error.py.

nodes.label: Per-cell Google Flights verification
nodes.rationale: Via fast-flights (3.x): real bookable prices with real adults/children counts in the requested currency, about one second per lookup. The result is cached and folded back into the board, which re-sorts: if a verified price is much worse than the estimate, that destination visibly drops, which is the whole point. Verified cells get a solid border and their card header switches from EST to LIVE. As you verify a card's cheapest cell its headline falls through to the next unverified estimate, so a card only settles once you verify the cells you care about. Treat the board as ranking and the click as truth.

nodes.label: fast-flights library
nodes.rationale: Python library wrapping Google Flights; needs no key. Version 3.x. Has parser bugs: reads only payload[3][0], discards itineraries, and crashes with a bare TypeError on routes Google does not serve.

nodes.label: Auto cross-check toggle
nodes.rationale: On by default. The board renders from Kiwi in seconds, then Auto cross-check quietly re-prices its cheapest cells on Google Flights in the background, upgrading them from KIWI to LIVE in place and re-sorting. This is precisely what catches per-cell calendar staleness. When both sources price a cell they agree closely (Varna 1,854 vs 1,853; Larnaca 980 exact).

nodes.label: Per-destination cell picking for verification
nodes.rationale: Cells are picked per destination, not cheapest-N overall: a flat cheapest-40 list sent all 40 slots to a single cheap city. Now it takes each destination's own cheapest few (AUTO_VERIFY_PER_DEST, 6) and interleaves them, capped at AUTO_VERIFY_CELLS (40).

nodes.label: unpriceable_destinations drop
nodes.rationale: Routes Google cannot price are skipped: TLV->Ramon (ETM) failed all 40 attempts, simply not in Google's data. cache.unpriceable_destinations() drops any destination with 3+ failures and no successes so the budget is never burned re-failing the same route; those cells keep their Kiwi price, which is the right answer.

nodes.label: Kiwi price-calendar per-cell staleness
nodes.source_location: Why a cell occasionally disagrees wildly
nodes.rationale: Kiwi's price calendar is a precomputed index and individual entries go stale. Measured vs Kiwi's own full search: 4 of 5 routes agree within 8%; Catania on an uncommon 16-night trip was off by 2x, and Google put it higher still. It is per-cell staleness on unusual trip lengths, not a scaling error: the calendar scales correctly with passengers (measured exactly x1/x2/x3/x5).

nodes.label: Fill live
nodes.source_location: Fill live: the actual answer to sparse data
nodes.rationale: Each card has a Fill live button that prices every cell in that destination's grid via Google Flights at 4 concurrent lookups (~50s for a 197-cell grid, taking Larnaca from 96 cached cells to 196 real ones). Solves both problems at once: 100% coverage AND true prices for the real passenger mix, with no API key and no third-party dependency. Results are written to the cache as they arrive, so a cancelled or crashed fill keeps what it got and re-running retries only the failed cells. Concurrency is FM_FILL_WORKERS (default 4); raise it cautiously because a Google block costs far more than the speed gains.

nodes.label: Travelpayouts grid strategy (endpoint choice)
nodes.rationale: Which endpoint fills a departure x return grid was measured against the live API, not taken from the docs. /v2/prices/latest gave 29 distinct pairs and up to 14 returns per departure, a strict superset of every other source on all 8 destinations tested, so there is nothing to gain from unioning them and it is the only strategy used. FM_GRID_STRATEGY (default 'latest'). Reproduce with data/probe_api.py, data/coverage.py, data/coverage_horizon.py.

nodes.label: /v2/prices/latest
nodes.rationale: The chosen grid-fill endpoint. Rows carry no booking link, so the Aviasales deeplink is constructed as /search/ORIGIN{DDMM}DEST{DDMM}{pax}.

nodes.label: /aviasales/v3/prices_for_dates
nodes.rationale: Still used for discovery, where omitting destination answers 'where can I go from here' in one call. It silently picks one arbitrary return date per departure unless you pass return_at, which is what made the first implementation return 1% coverage.

nodes.label: Destination discovery
nodes.rationale: Discovery ranks candidates on the cheapest fare anywhere in the month, not strictly inside the +/-7 window, because requiring an in-window row would discard destinations whose grid can still be filled. It over-fetches FM_CANDIDATE_MULTIPLIER (3.0) x candidates and stops once enough grids come back non-empty.

nodes.label: Aviasales deeplink construction
nodes.rationale: latest rows carry no booking link, so the Aviasales deeplink is constructed as /search/ORIGIN{DDMM}DEST{DDMM}{pax}. TRAVELPAYOUTS_MARKER is the affiliate marker appended to Aviasales links.

nodes.label: Diverging price colour ramp
nodes.rationale: A diverging price scale applied per matrix: green = destination's cheapest -> neutral -> red = its dearest. The arms are asymmetric on purpose: green<->red is the worst pair for red-green colour blindness (a symmetric ramp gives a deuteranopia deltaE of 1.5, indistinguishable). The green arm runs dark (OKLCH L 0.40) and the red arm light (L 0.70), lifting the worst mirrored pair to 7.1 so you can tell cheap from dear by lightness alone. Regenerate with data/emit_ramp_css.py; re-check CVD with data/check_diverging_cvd.py.

nodes.label: Reserved yellow marker
nodes.rationale: Each card's own cheapest cell gets a yellow ring; the board-wide cheapest gets a thicker ring plus a yellow card border. Yellow is reserved and never appears in the ramp, so the marker can never be read as a price level; that is also why the ramp's midpoint is neutral rather than yellow.

nodes.label: Per-step ramp ink colours
nodes.rationale: Each ramp step ships its own ink colour (--qi0..--qi6, black or white by measured contrast), because a diverging ramp has both ends dark and a single flip index cannot work. Minimum label contrast is 4.8:1. Every cell also carries its price as text and the table view lists everything, which is the real backstop.

nodes.label: CVD check (Machado-Oliveira-Fernandes)
nodes.source_location: The arms are asymmetric on purpose
nodes.rationale: Colour-vision-deficiency simulation at severity 1.0 for protanopia and deuteranopia, used to measure deltaE between mirrored ramp pairs. Run with data/check_diverging_cvd.py.

nodes.label: Previous sequential green ramp (superseded)
nodes.rationale: A sequential one-hue green ramp encoding cheapness: deepest green = cheapest, receding toward the surface as price rises. Steps generated by data/make_ramp.py in OKLCH at a fixed green hue with chroma pushed to just inside the sRGB gamut, because interpolating in sRGB desaturates the mid-steps to grey. It intentionally fails the ordinal light-end contrast check because a continuous sequential ramp is allowed to recede at its low end; the relief is that every cell carries a visible price label. --ramp-flip is the measured step at which cell ink switches (5 in light, 4 in dark).

nodes.label: Merged CA bundle (config._ca_bundle)
nodes.rationale: The corporate proxy intercepts some hosts and re-signs them with the internal CA, while others are reached directly and need the ordinary public roots. Neither bundle alone works for both, so config._ca_bundle() merges certifi with ~/certificates/amat-corporate-cas.pem into data/ca-merged.pem and uses that. Without the merge, api.travelpayouts.com works but pypi.org fails, or vice versa. Override with FM_CA_BUNDLE.

nodes.label: fast-flights install workaround
nodes.rationale: fast-flights cannot be installed with plain pip here: pip is pinned to an internal Artifactory mirror that does not carry it, and pip's own TLS stack fails against upstream PyPI. Reinstall after a Python upgrade with py -3 data/get_wheel.py fast-flights primp protobuf selectolax then pip install --no-index --find-links wheels fast-flights.

nodes.label: _parse_all_itineraries
nodes.rationale: fast-flights' parser reads only payload[3][0]. Google also returns a 'best flights' block at payload[2][0], and on TLV-LON that block held the cheapest option by a wide margin (Israir 8,285 ILS vs 10,974, a 24% understatement). _parse_all_itineraries in providers/google_flights.py reads every block and falls back to the library parser if Google changes shape.

nodes.label: parser_version / PARSER_VERSION invalidation
nodes.rationale: Verified rows carry parser_version; anything older than config.PARSER_VERSION is ignored and re-fetched, so a parser fix invalidates stale prices automatically instead of silently trusting them.

nodes.label: Rejected flight-source survey
nodes.source_location: Why not Skyscanner, Amadeus, Ryanair, or the airlines directly?
nodes.rationale: All investigated with live probes. Skyscanner: commercial partner application, no self-service key. Kiwi Tequila: invite-only since 2026, self-serve signup closed. Amadeus: self-service tier shut down July 2026. Duffel: booking-oriented, per-booking pricing. RapidAPI Skyscanner proxies: paid, unofficial scrapers against Skyscanner's terms, still only estimates. The conclusion: the best free source was the one already integrated (Google Flights, keyless, effectively unlimited, real family pricing).

nodes.label: Ryanair farfnd probe (data/probe_ryanair.py)
nodes.source_location: Why not Skyscanner, Amadeus, Ryanair, or the airlines directly?
nodes.rationale: The farfnd API is perfect (cheapest round trips to every destination over a date range, one call, keyless) but Ryanair serves zero Israeli airports (224 active, none in IL), so it is useless from TLV.

nodes.label: Wizz Air API probe (data/probe_wizz.py, probe_wizz2.py)
nodes.rationale: be.wizzair.com/<version>/Api works; the version must be scraped from their homepage bundle (29.15.1). asset/map gives 196 cities and 29 TLV destinations; search/timetable returns ~20 dated prices per leg per POST. Deliberately not wired in as a price source because the timetable returns a per-person lowest fare that ignores passenger counts, which would reintroduce the x5 extrapolation error that Fill live eliminates; it also rejects repeated calls with InvalidProtocol and its version string moves.

nodes.label: Israeli carrier feed probes (El Al, Arkia, Israir)
nodes.rationale: data/probe_il_carriers.py. El Al returns HTTP 247 (a WAF code) on any API path; Arkia shows a Cloudflare bot challenge on every path; Israir's only /api/* routes are CMS config, not flights. Google's own response for TLV-LON lists 33 carriers including El Al and Arkia, and filled cells already return Wizz Air, Israir and SKY express as cheapest-per-cell winners, so the missing piece was itineraries (our parser), not the source.

nodes.label: Demo mode (--demo / FM_DEMO)
nodes.rationale: Synthetic data, no token needed, good for a look around. FM_DEMO=1 for synthetic data.

nodes.label: backend/app.py
nodes.rationale: FastAPI, SSE streaming, /api/verify. Holds the in-memory _streams registry for search progress.

nodes.label: backend/board.py
nodes.rationale: discovery -> grid fill -> progressive events.

nodes.label: backend/cache.py
nodes.rationale: SQLite: cells, verified, searches. Exposes unpriceable_destinations().

nodes.label: backend/models.py
nodes.rationale: SearchRequest, Cell, DestinationMatrix.

nodes.label: backend/airports.py
nodes.rationale: IATA -> city/country (downloaded once, cached to airports.json).

nodes.label: backend/config.py
nodes.rationale: token, defaults, CA bundle resolution (_ca_bundle), PARSER_VERSION.

nodes.label: backend/providers/travelpayouts.py
nodes.rationale: board fill + destination discovery.

nodes.label: backend/providers/google_flights.py
nodes.rationale: live per-cell verification; contains _parse_all_itineraries.

nodes.label: backend/providers/demo.py
nodes.rationale: synthetic data for --demo.

nodes.label: frontend/ (index.html, app.js, styles.css)
nodes.rationale: The board UI: matrices, scroll viewports, colour ramp, filters, table view.

nodes.label: data/probe_api.py
nodes.rationale: which endpoint can fill a grid (measured).

nodes.label: data/make_ramp.py
nodes.rationale: derives the green sequential ramp.

nodes.label: data/estimate_error.py
nodes.rationale: reproduces the measured optimism of Travelpayouts family-total estimates vs Google Flights.

nodes.label: data/get_wheel.py
nodes.rationale: fetch a PyPI wheel past the pinned corporate mirror.
